functionalRequirements.title: User Registration and Profile Creation
functionalRequirements.description: Users (owners & walkers) must be able to register, create and manage their profiles with necessary personal and pet/service details.

functionalRequirements.title: Walker Search and Filtering
functionalRequirements.description: Pet owners must be able to search for available dog walkers based on location, availability, services offered, ratings, and specific pet needs.

functionalRequirements.title: Service Booking and Scheduling
functionalRequirements.description: Pet owners must be able to book a dog walking service for a specific date, time, and duration. Walkers must be able to accept or decline bookings.

functionalRequirements.title: Real-time Walk Tracking (GPS)
functionalRequirements.description: Pet owners must be able to track their dog's walk in real-time on a map within the app once the walk has started.

functionalRequirements.title: In-app Messaging
functionalRequirements.description: Pet owners and walkers must be able to communicate securely through an in-app chat feature before, during, and after a booking.

functionalRequirements.title: Secure Payment Processing
functionalRequirements.description: The app must support secure in-app payments from pet owners to walkers, including service fees and tip options.

functionalRequirements.title: Rating and Review System
functionalRequirements.description: Both pet owners and walkers must be able to rate and review each other after a service is completed.

functionalRequirements.title: Walker Background Checks and Verification
functionalRequirements.description: The platform must implement a process for comprehensive background checks and identity verification for all prospective dog walkers.

functionalRequirements.title: Push Notifications for Key Events
functionalRequirements.description: Users must receive real-time push notifications for booking confirmations, walk start/end, messages, and emergencies.

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Response Time
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The application should load within 3 seconds and API responses should be received within 500ms under normal load.

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: User Capacity
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The system must be able to support at least 100,000 active users and 10,000 concurrent active walks without performance degradation.

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Data Protection and Privacy
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: All user data, especially payment and personal information, must be encrypted in transit and at rest, complying with GDPR/CCPA regulations.

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Uptime
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform should maintain an uptime of 99.9% to ensure continuous service availability.

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Intuitive User Interface
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The mobile application must have an intuitive and easy-to-navigate interface, minimizing user onboarding time and errors.

data.overview: The database design utilizes PostgreSQL as the primary relational database, chosen for its robustness, ACID compliance, and strong support for complex queries and geographical data (PostGIS extension). It will store all core application data including user profiles, pets, bookings, transactions, and reviews. Redis will be used as an in-memory data store for caching, session management, and real-time data like active walk locations.

designDecisions: Use UUIDs for primary keys to ensure global uniqueness and prevent sequential ID guessing.

Separate `users` from `owner_profiles` and `walker_profiles` to allow a single user account to potentially switch roles or have multiple roles in the future (though initial focus is one primary role per user).
Utilize PostGIS extension for `walker_profiles.location` to enable efficient geospatial queries for walker search.
Store sensitive data like passwords as hashes, not plain text.
Implement foreign key constraints for data integrity across related tables.
Use `JSON` type for flexible storage of `services_offered` and `rates` in `walker_profiles` to accommodate varying service structures.
Maintain `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps on most tables for auditing and change tracking.
Add indexes strategically on frequently queried fields and foreign keys to optimize read performance.
data.scalingStrategy: Database scaling will involve vertical scaling initially for PostgreSQL (more powerful instance), followed by horizontal scaling using read replicas for analytics and reporting. For writes, techniques like sharding or partitioning will be considered as the user base grows significantly, potentially by geographic region. Redis will scale horizontally as needed.

data.overview: The system architecture is a microservices-oriented monolith for the MVP, consisting of a React Native mobile application communicating with a Node.js/Express.js backend API. PostgreSQL serves as the primary data store, with Redis for caching and real-time operations. AI features will be integrated as separate services, accessible via the main backend. All user interactions and real-time events are mediated through a robust API gateway.

frontend.stateManagement: Redux Toolkit (with Redux Thunk for async actions)

aiService.architecture: AI models will be deployed as separate microservices (e.g., using Python/Flask or AWS Lambda functions) and accessed by the main Node.js backend via REST API calls. This allows for independent scaling and technology choice for AI components.
models: Smart Walker Matching (Collaborative Filtering / Content-Based Recommendation)
Dynamic Pricing (Regression Model with real-time features)
pipeline: Model Training (offline batch or online learning)
aiService.infrastructure: AWS SageMaker for model development and training, deployed as AWS Lambda or EC2 instances for inference, or a dedicated Python microservice.

deployment.scaling: Backend will utilize AWS EC2 Auto Scaling Groups behind an Application Load Balancer. PostgreSQL will use AWS RDS for managed scaling and failover. Redis will use AWS ElastiCache. All services will be containerized with Docker for consistent deployment.

security.authentication: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for stateless authentication. Passwords will be securely hashed (e.g., bcrypt).
security.authorization: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) middleware checks user roles and permissions for each API endpoint.
dataProtection: Sensitive data (e.g., payment info, personally identifiable information) encrypted at rest in the database.
Regular security audits and vulnerability scanning.
Secure storage of API keys and credentials using AWS Secrets Manager or environment variables.
compliance: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) for payment handling (via Stripe integration).

strengths: Robust relational database design with clear entities and relationships, well-suited for a marketplace model.
Comprehensive API design covering core functionalities, authentication, and admin needs, with good consideration for rate limiting and authorization.
Strategic use of industry-standard technologies (React Native, Node.js, PostgreSQL, AWS) ensuring scalability, maintainability, and access to a large talent pool.
Early integration of AI features for core business value (matching, anomaly detection) sets the product apart.
Detailed roadmap with clear phases, milestones, and specific deliverables provides a solid plan for execution.
Strong emphasis on security (JWT, RBAC, encryption) and compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI DSS).
Well-defined testing strategy covering unit, integration, and E2E tests, crucial for a high-trust application.
weaknesses: Initial monolith approach for the backend, while good for MVP, may become a bottleneck if not refactored into microservices as complexity grows.
Reliance on third-party services (payments, background checks) introduces external dependencies and potential vendor lock-in.
AI features, while valuable, are high complexity and could significantly impact the initial development timeline if not carefully scoped and managed.
Real-time GPS tracking and messaging can be resource-intensive and require careful optimization to handle high concurrency.
Scalability strategy for PostgreSQL, while outlined, will require significant architectural changes (sharding) for extreme scale, which is a future consideration but a known challenge.
missingComponents: Detailed schema for real-time messaging data (could be stored in PostgreSQL or a dedicated chat service like Firebase/Twilio Conversations).

- ✓ Comprehensive API design covering core functionalities, authentication, and admin needs, with good consideration for rate limiting and authorization.
- ✓ Strategic use of industry-standard technologies (React Native, Node.js, PostgreSQL, AWS) ensuring scalability, maintainability, and access to a large talent pool.
- ✓ Early integration of AI features for core business value (matching, anomaly detection) sets the product apart.
- ✓ Detailed roadmap with clear phases, milestones, and specific deliverables provides a solid plan for execution.
- ✓ Strong emphasis on security (JWT, RBAC, encryption) and compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI DSS).
- ✓ Well-defined testing strategy covering unit, integration, and E2E tests, crucial for a high-trust application.

#### Risks & Weaknesses
- ⚠️ Initial monolith approach for the backend, while good for MVP, may become a bottleneck if not refactored into microservices as complexity grows.
- ⚠️ Reliance on third-party services (payments, background checks) introduces external dependencies and potential vendor lock-in.
- ⚠️ AI features, while valuable, are high complexity and could significantly impact the initial development timeline if not carefully scoped and managed.
- ⚠️ Real-time GPS tracking and messaging can be resource-intensive and require careful optimization to handle high concurrency.
- ⚠️ Scalability strategy for PostgreSQL, while outlined, will require significant architectural changes (sharding) for extreme scale, which is a future consideration but a known challenge.

#### Suggested Improvements
- → Consider a dedicated real-time messaging service (e.g., Firebase, PubNub, or self-hosted Socket.IO cluster) rather than a purely API-based chat for better scalability and performance.
- → Establish clear SLAs and monitoring for all third-party integrations to manage external dependencies.
- → For AI features, start with simpler heuristic-based solutions for MVP and iterate towards more complex ML models post-launch, or use managed AI services (e.g., AWS Personalize) to reduce operational overhead.
- → Plan for database partitioning/sharding from early stages, even if not implemented immediately, to prepare for future growth.
- → Implement a robust centralized logging system (e.g., ELK stack, Datadog) and incident management process.
- → Explore GraphQL for the API layer to offer more flexible data fetching for clients, especially with multiple profile types and complex relationships.

designDecisions: Use UUIDs for primary keys to ensure global uniqueness and prevent sequential ID guessing.

Separate `users` from `owner_profiles` and `walker_profiles` to allow a single user account to potentially switch roles or have multiple roles in the future (though initial focus is one primary role per user).
Utilize PostGIS extension for `walker_profiles.location` to enable efficient geospatial queries for walker search.
Store sensitive data like passwords as hashes, not plain text.
Implement foreign key constraints for data integrity across related tables.
Use `JSON` type for flexible storage of `services_offered` and `rates` in `walker_profiles` to accommodate varying service structures.
Maintain `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps on most tables for auditing and change tracking.
Add indexes strategically on frequently queried fields and foreign keys to optimize read performance.
data.scalingStrategy: Database scaling will involve vertical scaling initially for PostgreSQL (more powerful instance), followed by horizontal scaling using read replicas for analytics and reporting. For writes, techniques like sharding or partitioning will be considered as the user base grows significantly, potentially by geographic region. Redis will scale horizontally as needed.

data.overview: The system architecture is a microservices-oriented monolith for the MVP, consisting of a React Native mobile application communicating with a Node.js/Express.js backend API. PostgreSQL serves as the primary data store, with Redis for caching and real-time operations. AI features will be integrated as separate services, accessible via the main backend. All user interactions and real-time events are mediated through a robust API gateway.

frontend.stateManagement: Redux Toolkit (with Redux Thunk for async actions)

aiService.architecture: AI models will be deployed as separate microservices (e.g., using Python/Flask or AWS Lambda functions) and accessed by the main Node.js backend via REST API calls. This allows for independent scaling and technology choice for AI components.
models: Smart Walker Matching (Collaborative Filtering / Content-Based Recommendation)
Dynamic Pricing (Regression Model with real-time features)
pipeline: Model Training (offline batch or online learning)
aiService.infrastructure: AWS SageMaker for model development and training, deployed as AWS Lambda or EC2 instances for inference, or a dedicated Python microservice.

deployment.scaling: Backend will utilize AWS EC2 Auto Scaling Groups behind an Application Load Balancer. PostgreSQL will use AWS RDS for managed scaling and failover. Redis will use AWS ElastiCache. All services will be containerized with Docker for consistent deployment.

security.authentication: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for stateless authentication. Passwords will be securely hashed (e.g., bcrypt).
security.authorization: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) middleware checks user roles and permissions for each API endpoint.
dataProtection: Sensitive data (e.g., payment info, personally identifiable information) encrypted at rest in the database.
Regular security audits and vulnerability scanning.
Secure storage of API keys and credentials using AWS Secrets Manager or environment variables.
compliance: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) for payment handling (via Stripe integration).

strengths: Robust relational database design with clear entities and relationships, well-suited for a marketplace model.
Comprehensive API design covering core functionalities, authentication, and admin needs, with good consideration for rate limiting and authorization.
Strategic use of industry-standard technologies (React Native, Node.js, PostgreSQL, AWS) ensuring scalability, maintainability, and access to a large talent pool.
Early integration of AI features for core business value (matching, anomaly detection) sets the product apart.
Detailed roadmap with clear phases, milestones, and specific deliverables provides a solid plan for execution.
Strong emphasis on security (JWT, RBAC, encryption) and compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI DSS).
Well-defined testing strategy covering unit, integration, and E2E tests, crucial for a high-trust application.
weaknesses: Initial monolith approach for the backend, while good for MVP, may become a bottleneck if not refactored into microservices as complexity grows.
Reliance on third-party services (payments, background checks) introduces external dependencies and potential vendor lock-in.
AI features, while valuable, are high complexity and could significantly impact the initial development timeline if not carefully scoped and managed.
Real-time GPS tracking and messaging can be resource-intensive and require careful optimization to handle high concurrency.
Scalability strategy for PostgreSQL, while outlined, will require significant architectural changes (sharding) for extreme scale, which is a future consideration but a known challenge.
missingComponents: Detailed schema for real-time messaging data (could be stored in PostgreSQL or a dedicated chat service like Firebase/Twilio Conversations).
Specific plan for internationalization/localization if expanding beyond initial urban areas.
Comprehensive error logging and monitoring strategy beyond just 'LoggingMiddleware'.
More detailed disaster recovery plan for critical data beyond just 'backup'.
Specific details on image/video processing (e.g., resizing, compression) for S3 uploads.
Web portal for pet owners (current plan is mobile-only, which is a constraint but also a missing component for broader access).
suggestedImprovements: Consider a dedicated real-time messaging service (e.g., Firebase, PubNub, or self-hosted Socket.IO cluster) rather than a purely API-based chat for better scalability and performance.
Establish clear SLAs and monitoring for all third-party integrations to manage external dependencies.

For AI features, start with simpler heuristic-based solutions for MVP and iterate towards more complex ML models post-launch, or use managed AI services (e.g., AWS Personalize) to reduce operational overhead.
Plan for database partitioning/sharding from early stages, even if not implemented immediately, to prepare for future growth.
Implement a robust centralized logging system (e.g., ELK stack, Datadog) and incident management process.
Explore GraphQL for the API layer to offer more flexible data fetching for clients, especially with multiple profile types and complex relationships.
